name: University of Bath

settingEvidence.evidence: We are a campus university in the South West of England and offer courses in engineering, humanities, management, science and social science.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students on standard full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28). Bath says the 2027/28 regulated fee is still to be confirmed by the UK government (subject to parliamentary approval); placement/study-abroad year fees are reduced.

source.evidence: Home UK tuition fees are £10,050 for standard full-time courses in 2027/28.

livingCosts.text: University self-catered (non-catered) halls cost about £98–£315 a week including bills, average £183 a week (2026/27). Bath's sample student budget for a 38-week year totals about £12,392.

source.evidence: *University Non-Catered Accommodation (ranges from £98-£315 per week) Average cost £183 p/w. inclusive of bills

openDays.text: Next in-person undergraduate open days are in June 2027 (exact dates not announced yet).

source.evidence: Our next in-person Open Days are in June 2027.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Bath's contextual criteria automatically get a lower contextual offer and extra consideration from an Admissions Progression Team.
contextual.typicalReduction: Two grades lower than the typical entry requirements for most courses (Economics & Mathematics: one grade lower for 2026 and 2027 entry).

criteria.detail: Recorded as eligible for Free School Meals in the National Pupil Database (England, or equivalent in NI/Wales) at any point during Key Stage 3 or Key Stage 4. FSM during sixth form does not count.

Home postcode when you apply is in an area of high socio-economic disadvantage (IMD quintiles 1 or 2) and you attended a UK state school or college for at least two full academic years in your last four years.
Care leaver or care experienced, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
Young carer, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
Estranged student, aged 25 or under when you start, with evidence.
You hold leave in the UK as a refugee, asylum seeker or person with humanitarian protection, or you are the child of someone who does.

contextual.rulesText: You will be considered for contextual admissions (including contextual offers) if you are eligible for UK fees and meet any one of the criteria. Contextual offers are automatic and replace the typical or alternative offers; contextual and alternative offers do not stack.

source.evidence: You will be considered for contextual admissions (including contextual offers) if you are a student eligible for UK fees and you meet any one of the following criteria:

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-17: bath.ac.uk/courses/undergraduate-2028/ returns 404), so all courses use 2027 entry.
Bath does not use the TMUA (or MAT) for any course from 2025 entry.

Economics selection (A level applicants) is weighted: GCSE profile 50% (best eight grades incl. Maths and English), predicted grades 20%, subjects 20%, personal statement 10%. Geography and Psychology are both on the Economics preferred-subject list.
Bath accepts all A levels equally; no more than three A levels are ever needed and extra subjects give no advantage.
Alternative offers (EPQ, extra maths) never lower the offer by more than one grade; contextual and alternative offers do not stack (contextual applicants get only the contextual offer).
Guaranteed conditional offers for students who complete Pathway to Bath, Discover Bath or Bath Ambitions are published for 2026 and 2027 entry; terms for 2028 entry are not yet published.
Bath also pledges guaranteed offers to care leavers and estranged students who meet its criteria.
Student Performance Sport Offer Scheme: nominated student athletes who meet the criteria get an alternative offer one grade below the typical offer.
Most offers are made in February and March, after the January UCAS equal consideration deadline (13 January 2027 for 2027 entry).
